description: A FILE value may not be a GROUP BY, ORDER BY or PARTITION BY key, may not be ordered by MAX / MIN / MODE, may not be concatenated, and may not be cast or converted to anything - each with its own live-measured sentence. The key rejections name the clause ('Expressions of type FILE cannot be used as GROUP BY keys'), the ordering aggregates use the 'does not support FILE argument type' form, concatenation uses the argument-type list, and every CAST names the CONVERSION FUNCTION it desugars to rather than the cast itself - CAST(f AS FLOAT) is reported against TO_DOUBLE and CAST(f AS TIMESTAMP) against TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ, with the target's full declared width. The accepted half is pinned just as hard: a FILE still compares, de-duplicates, joins, takes part in UNION and IN, feeds the non-ordering aggregates and windows, passes through the conditionals and containers, and its ACCESSOR results are ordinary keys that group and sort freely. An OBJECT column groups, sorts and casts to VARCHAR perfectly well, so none of these rejections may be widened to semi-structured values in general. Converted 1:1 from functions/file/FileKeyAndCastRejectionTest (now retired); the class's @BeforeEach built the fk table with its FILE/OBJECT/VARCHAR control columns, which each converted test recreates as its first three steps.
